newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen edging higher, peso firm.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen edging higher, peso firm.

text.p: Traders saw Mexican stocks opening mixed to moderately up on Tuesday, with an expected early surge on Wall Street finding only a pale echo in Mexico due to poor first quarter earnings reports.
"It will be very quiet here, earnings have not been very good. We may see some selective technical rebounds, but not much upside on the whole," one desk trader said.

Traders said they expected the peso to open firm in response to an early plunge in U.S. long bond yields, and said jitters remained in the market over U.S. data to be released later in the week, and thus saw a wide trading range.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.9400/8.0000 per dollar for the benchmark 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9470/7.9520 per dollar, compared to Monday's close of 7.9700/7.9800.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening stable on quiet trade in line with expected firmness on the peso, dealers said.
